summary: Extracted the S007 decide()/reconcile logic out of bot/s007_paper.py::live() into a reusable run_cycle_for_account(creds, preset, risk_pct, fixed_lot, use_fixed_lot, magic, logger, ...) function, parameterized instead of hardcoded to bot.s007_config globals; live() now just calls it with the module defaults, so the single-account CLI behaviour is unchanged (verified via --dry-run regression). Rewrote webapp/runner.py for the new broker-agnostic multi-strategy schema (User/Account/AccountStrategy/Strategy) as a coordinator+worker pair: "python -m webapp.runner --strategy S007" loads enabled AccountStrategy rows and spawns one worker subprocess per account (because CTraderAdapter drives its session through a single reactor.run() call -- Twisted reactors cannot be restarted in the same process, so parallel accounts within one tick require one OS process each, not threads/asyncio); a worker runs exactly one cycle for one account_strategy id and exits. Curated events (cycle_start/cycle_end/position_open/position_close/error) now also write to the DB logs table via webapp/schemas/logs.py; full per-tick debug detail (and the label_was_opened/closed dedup state decide() depends on) still goes to per-account utils.trade_logger.StrategyLogger JSONL files under reports/logs/ -- NOT yet safe to drop for containerization, since that dedup state currently only lives in those files (open item). Rewrote webapp/cli.py for the same new schema (init-db/create-user/add-account/add-strategy/link-strategy/enable/disable/list), reusing webapp/schemas/ for validation. S009/Bybit multi-account support deliberately NOT done here: bot/s009_paper.py keeps its ledger state in one shared file for the whole strategy (load_state/save_state), not per (account, strategy), so it would need its own refactor before it could run several accounts in parallel the same way.

Added docs/DEV_PLANS.md, a new dev-plans doc capturing the decided multi-account Docker migration architecture (stateless-tick scheduling, per-strategy job granularity, DB-as-source-of-truth, DB schema decisions, logging split, Alembic migration convention, accounts.yml import mapping) and its current build status, so this is tracked in-repo instead of only in Claude memory. Created 1 User, 2 Strategy rows (S007/CTRADER, S009/BYBIT), 2 Account rows (CTRADER demo, BYBIT mainnet), and 2 AccountStrategy links with initial_balance seeded from accounts.yml. APP_SECRET_KEY must be exported from .env manually before running this script -- it does not load .env itself, same as the rest of webapp/.

Tested the new webapp.runner (coordinator+worker subprocess-per-account) end to end against the real DB-migrated S007/CTRADER account: coordinator found 1 enabled account_strategy row, spawned a worker, worker decrypted DB credentials, ran a full cTrader reconcile cycle, and wrote cycle_start/cycle_end to both the file logger and the DB logs table; account_strategies.status/last_cycle_at updated correctly. Uninstalled the old single-account launchd job (com.anton.algo.s007bot) now that the DB-driven runner path works. Two initial worker runs appeared to hang (55s+ with no output) -- root-caused to stdout full-buffering in a non-TTY subprocess hiding progress, combined with what looks like transient cTrader demo-server slowness, not a code bug: two subsequent clean runs completed in ~7s, matching the old single-account path.

Load-tested the multi-account parallel fan-out with two throwaway benchmark scripts (not committed): (1) N mocked no-network workers (Python startup + one DB query each) scale well -- N=40 parallel finishes in ~1.8s wall time, so coordinator/DB overhead is not the bottleneck. (2) N real concurrent cTrader demo-server sessions against the SAME account/client_id: N=5 all succeed in ~4.2s; N=10 mostly succeed at ~4.6s but one session stalled to 36.8s; N=15 failed to complete within 90s (at least one session hung indefinitely). This points at the cTrader DEMO server itself, not our code, as the scaling limit for near-simultaneous sessions on one account/client_id -- unclear if this generalizes to N DIFFERENT accounts/client_ids in production (untested, no second real account available). Suggests staggering worker starts and/or adding retry-with-backoff in run_worker() before scaling account count up.

Follow-up load test isolating our own fan-out/DB overhead from the cTrader demo-server bottleneck found in the previous test: a throwaway mock worker (sleeps a fixed 5s to simulate broker latency, then does the same DB read+write pattern run_worker() does against the real sqlite DB, no real network) scales cleanly -- N=20/50/100/200 parallel workers all succeed with wall times of 5.7s/7.0s/8.9s/14.1s and no outlier tail latency (max per-worker ~9s even at N=200). Confirms the coordinator/subprocess-fan-out/SQLite-write design is NOT the bottleneck for scaling account count; the earlier-found slowdown (some sessions stalling to 30s+ at N=10 real broker connections) is specific to the cTrader demo server handling concurrent sessions on one account/client_id, not our architecture. Still unverified: whether that broker-side limit is per-account, per-client_id, or per-IP -- matters for whether it actually constrains production (different users -> different client_ids). Needs testing with a second real distinct account once available.

Rewrote webapp/app.py (FastAPI dashboard) for the broker-agnostic multi-strategy schema, replacing the old single-strategy version that referenced removed fields (User.ctrader_client_id/.client_secret/.access_token, Account.ctid_trader_account_id/.preset/.risk_pct/.is_live/.strategy). Routes: /accounts/add (broker-conditional credential form, validated via webapp/schemas AccountCreate), /accounts/{id}/link-strategy (attach a Strategy to an Account with its own preset/risk/lot, validated via AccountStrategyCreate), /account-strategies/{id}/toggle|save|unlink (per link, not per account, since one account can run several strategies), /users admin page. Journal page (/journal) + per-(account,strategy) trading dashboard (/account-strategies/{id}); fixed two real bugs found while testing.
details: Added GET /journal with two tabs: 'events' over the logs table (filters: account, strategy, level, kind; 50/page) and 'positions' over the full Position history incl. closed (filters: account, strategy, status). Both are scoped to the caller: events by user_id OR account_id in the user's accounts, positions by account_id in the user's accounts; a foreign account_id in the query string is ignored rather than honoured. Added GET /account-strategies/{lid} -- a detail page for one (account, strategy) pair: total/open/closed counts, buy-vs-sell, add(pyramid) share, avg + median hold time, close-reason breakdown with bars, a 30-day opened-per-day sparkline, last 20 positions, last 20 log entries, and an errors-in-24h counter. Stats are computed in plain Python in _link_stats() over the rows already fetched -- the volume is tiny and it keeps the SQL trivial. DELIBERATELY NO PnL: the positions table stores entry/sl/tp only -- no exit price, no volume, no realised result -- so any money figure would be invented. PnL waits until the runner writes close prices; the page says so in-line so nobody assumes it was forgotten. New templates journal.html + strategy_detail.html; base.html gained a Journal nav link and CSS for .stat-grid/.stat/.bar/.tabs/.filters/.lvl-*; dashboard.html now links the strategy name to its detail page. Both routes are read-only over DB state -- no broker calls, per the UI<->runner decoupling rule. BUG FIX 1 (security/validation): CtraderCredentials/BybitCredentials fields were bare `str`, so an add-account form with every credential field blank validated fine and created a broken account that would only fail later inside a runner cycle. All five fields now carry Field(min_length=1). BUG FIX 2 (flash messages): flash() did session.setdefault('_flash', []).append(...), mutating the list in place. Starlette's Session only sets `modified` on __setitem__/__delitem__, so the cookie was not re-sent and EVERY flash after the first one in a session was silently dropped. flash() now rebuilds the list and reassigns session['_flash']. Verified by an extended out-of-tree smoke test (38 checks, TestClient against a seeded throwaway sqlite with 60 historical positions and 70 log entries): pagination, every filter, empty-result and out-of-range pages, a bogus link id, cross-user access, and both bug fixes. All pass.

summary: Position sync from the broker (webapp/sync_positions.py) + migration 002 (9 PnL/origin columns) + real PnL in the UI.
details: New webapp/sync_positions.py refreshes the DB from cTrader so `positions` reflects broker reality: open rows get real entry price, current SL/TP and volume; rows that vanished from the broker are closed with reason='broker_closed' and priced from the deal list; broker positions we do not know are ADOPTED as new rows with origin='adopted'. Scope chosen by the user: cTrader/S007 only (Bybit returns only {symbol: net qty} with no label or id, so its rows cannot be matched to specific Position records). Matching is TWO-TIER -- broker_position_id first, label second; label-only matching was a real bug caught by the unit test, since an adopted row's label ('adopted:<id>') is ours and is never echoed back by the broker, so every pass closed a position that was still open. Architecture: runner-side, never UI-side (app.py still imports no broker code). Because CTraderAdapter drives Twisted's reactor and a reactor can only run() once per process, the sync runs in a subprocess (spawn_sync_worker) -- the runner cannot sync in-process after a cycle. runner.py calls it at the end of each cycle with the leftover tick budget (SYNC_BUDGET_S=25, skipped below MIN_SYNC_BUDGET_S=8); the sync can never change the cycle's exit code. Migration 002 adds origin, exit_price, volume_lots, gross_profit, swap, commission, pnl, broker_deal_id, synced_at and widens broker_position_id INTEGER->BIGINT (cTrader positionId is an int64). Verified upgrade->downgrade->upgrade on sqlite. UI: _link_stats gained a money block (realised PnL, win rate, profit factor, avg win/loss, best/worst, max drawdown, equity) computed ONLY over closed rows with a non-NULL pnl -- NULL means 'unknown / not synced', never 0.0, so unpriced rows are counted and reported separately and render as '--'. Adopted positions carry a badge; their money counts, their hold times do not. New LogKinds: sync, position_adopted. Tested by tests/webapp/test_sync_positions.py (6 scenarios, ~39 checks, no network, throwaway sqlite) and by the out-of-tree TestClient smoke test. NOT yet done: migration 002 must be applied to the real DB by the user.

summary: Removed the implicit init_db()/create_all() call from webapp/app.py import time (Alembic-only schema ownership); moved the orphaned webapp/templates/creds.html to _to_delete/.
details: webapp/app.py called init_db() (Base.metadata.create_all()) unconditionally at module import time, i.e. on every web process start -- this let the FastAPI process silently create/patch schema behind Alembic's back on a DB that hadn't been migrated, which is exactly what webapp/cli.py's own cmd_init_db() docstring already warns against ('a dev/test convenience and does not know about Alembic's version table'). Removed the import and the call; a fresh dev DB now needs an explicit 'python -m webapp.cli init-db' or 'alembic -c webapp/alembic.ini upgrade head' before the app will find its tables -- same bootstrap step already required in practice, just no longer silently papered over. webapp/templates/creds.html referenced removed User.ctrader_client_id/.client_secret/.access_token fields and had no route rendering it (the old per-user /creds page was removed 2026-08-01 when credentials moved to Account) -- confirmed via grep with no remaining references, moved (not deleted, no rm in the bridge VM) to _to_delete/creds.html.dead_unused_2026-08-07. summary: Added the Docker/Ofelia scaffold for the DB-driven multi-account runner (docs/DEV_PLANS.md's 'one job per STRATEGY' design): a single worker image (Dockerfile + requirements-docker.txt, split from the research-only requirements.txt) runs `python -m webapp.runner --strategy <NAME>` per Ofelia job-run tick; only S007 is wired into a schedule so far ('* 10-16 * * 1-5', mirroring scripts/s007_tick.py's in_session() window). Verified end-to-end on this machine's Podman (not Docker) setup: image builds cleanly after loosening the cryptography/pyOpenSSL/service-identity pins (the exact local-venv trio was mutually unresolvable from a clean install), a one-off container run against the real demo account round-tripped through the bind-mounted data/app.db and reports/logs correctly, and Ofelia registers/runs the labeled job. Podman-machine specific fix documented in docker-compose.yml: bind-mount /run/podman/podman.sock (not the macOS-side /var/run/docker.sock forward) read-write, plus security_opt label=disable to clear an SELinux AVC denial on Fedora CoreOS (enforcing by default) that otherwise blocks the socket connect even as container root. Did not touch webapp/runner.py's S007-only dispatch, S009, or the legacy launchd job -- scoped to standing up the framework itself.

Generalized webapp/runner.py's strategy dispatch from a hardcoded S007-only check to a STRATEGY_WORKERS registry ({'S007': _worker_s007, 'S009': _worker_s009}), and refactored bot/s009_paper.py so S009 can run multi-account through it: extracted run_cycle_for_account(account_key, creds, state, logger, ...) from run_once()'s body (mirrors bot/s007_paper.py's function of the same name/shape), parameterized by an injectable state store instead of the single global reports/paper_s009/state.json. Added migration 003 (strategy_state table, one JSON blob per account_strategy_id) + webapp/state_store.py::DBStateStore for the DB-driven path, and utils/strategy_state.py::FileStateStore (extracted load_state/save_state) for the unchanged single-account CLI path -- run_once()/--status/--loop/scripts/s009_tick.py keep writing the same file, byte-for-byte, verified via a real --status read after the refactor. _worker_s009 hardcodes broker='off'/allow_mainnet=False deliberately -- enabling real orders through the DB-driven path is a separate future decision, not a side effect. Verified end-to-end against a throwaway copy of the real DB: `webapp.runner --worker --account-strategy-id 3` (Bybit-algo009) correctly wrote a strategy_state row and updated account_strategies.status, with zero broker orders. 55 new+existing tests pass (10 bot, 13 webapp, 32 scripts).

Added a day-done short-circuit to webapp/runner.py's DB-driven S007 worker: unlike the legacy scripts/s007_tick.py (loop_settled/loop_resumed guard), _worker_s007 used to open a real cTrader/Twisted session on every dispatcher tick for the rest of the session window even after the day's target was already reached. Fixed by stamping link.status = 'settled:<local date>' once a cycle comes back day_done/filtered/manual_stop, and returning immediately -- before constructing any creds/logger/broker session -- on a later same-day tick. Self-resetting: a new day's first tick has a stale date in status and runs normally, no separate reset needed. Also refreshed webapp/README.md (mostly already current from other work; added sections on the STRATEGY_WORKERS registry, S009's shadow-only DB-driven state, and the deployment/schedule.yml + scripts/scheduler_tick.py + Docker/Ofelia scheduling layer, none of which were documented there yet) and confirmed the empty _to_delete/ directory is already gone (git doesn't track empty dirs).

Fixed a real-money bug found while checking bot status: run_cycle_for_account() constructed BybitExec without ever passing env, so it always fell back to the BYBIT_TESTNET OS env var -- unset in the Ofelia dispatch container (not in docker-compose.ymls environment list, and .env is deliberately excluded from the image per .dockerignore with a since-stale bind-mount comment that was never implemented). Result: every DB-driven S009 cycle for Bybit-algo009 (a real-money MAINNET account, broker_mode=execute) silently hit api-testnet.bybit.com with its mainnet-only API key, 401ing (API key is invalid) and completely failing the cycle -- no rebalance, no equity read, nothing -- for about 17h (2026-08-13 21:05 UTC through 2026-08-14 14:xx UTC when this was caught), even though _worker_s009 already computed allow_mainnet from acc.env correctly (that only gates ORDER PLACEMENT, not which base URL/credential namespace BybitExec talks to). Added env: str | None = None to run_cycle_for_account, threaded through to both BybitExec(...) constructor call sites, and _worker_s009 now passes env=acc.env. Added regression tests in both tests/bot/test_s009_paper.py and tests/webapp/test_runner_s009.py (the existing allow_mainnet-focused tests never asserted on env at all -- confirmed both new tests fail against the pre-fix code and pass after). (1) New preset WORKING_S007_NEWSSAFE_MAX8_BE05 = NEWSSAFE_MAX8.with_(breakeven_at_r=0.5) -- verified dataclass-equal to run_s007_propscheme.py's winning ad-hoc combo (Gate 3: 100.0% cashout / 0.0% daily-bust). (2) Live breakeven: ProtoOAAmendPositionSLTPReq wired into bot/ctrader_s007.py (_amend_position_sltp_step, standalone amend_position_sl, 'amend' action kind in run_live_cycle using full_symbol.digits rounding). Trigger is the ENGINE's own be_moved flag surfaced through plan_now() (bot/s007_signals.py) -- same code path as the backtest, live/backtest can never disagree on WHEN; the amend targets the broker's ACTUAL fill price (have[lab]['price']) so real breakeven includes slippage; current takeProfit is always passed back because the amend message REPLACES both protection levels (unset TP would strip it). One-shot without extra state: decide() only amends when the current broker SL is strictly worse than the fill (buy: cur_sl<fill, sell: cur_sl>fill), so successful amends and manually-tightened stops are natural no-ops; failed amends retry next cycle. Added a sequential pipeline (e2e) test suite for S007: a stateful fake cTrader broker (fills, server-side SL/TP execution, deal history) drives the REAL engine (simulate_day) through the REAL live wiring (plan_now -> decide -> run_cycle_for_account -> webapp.runner._worker_s007/DB) cycle-by-cycle across a simulated trading day, instead of each layer being tested in isolation against a hand-scripted stub of the layer below. Covers 35 cases across three catalogs: engine/signal shapes (A1-A15, e.g. A/B scenarios, b_reversal_to_A, breakeven, EOD flatten, ghost trades), decide()/sizing/day-cap wiring (B1-B20, e.g. risk sizing, min-lot floor overshoot, day count/$ caps, slippage-aware risk accounting, manual stop, broker/session error isolation), and the DB-driven runner (C1-C6, e.g. Position row lifecycle, settled-status stamping, multi-account cap isolation). No production code was changed; two informational (non-bug) findings were noted for a human to review: engine day_done tracks only the primary leg's target, not a winning recovery leg, and a very low daily_risk_cap_pct/risk_pct ratio floors max_positions_per_day to 0, masking the $ cap check behind the count cap.

cTrader OAuth2 access-token auto-refresh, implemented ONCE in the shared broker client and wired into S011 only (Anton: 'если надо для этого брокера сделать глобально - переноси запросы на клиент для этой стратегии... чтобы CTrader работал для всех одинаково' + 'и используй клиент пока только для 011'). Motivated by the live outage found in this session's S011 diagnosis: 2026-09-21 00:00 -> 2026-09-22 09:45, 130 consecutive cycles failed with CH_ACCESS_TOKEN_INVALID, and as a knock-on the ESTOXX50/DOW exit signalled 18.09 was rejected MARKET_CLOSED and only executed 4 days late. There was NO refresh mechanism before this: scripts/ctrader_oauth.py printed the refreshToken with an explicit 'not currently used, no auto-refresh wired up' note, and no grant_type=refresh_token call existed anywhere. (1) NEW bot/clients/ctrader/auth.py -- Twisted-free OAuth2 token layer: TokenBundle (access/refresh/expires_at, needs_refresh() with REFRESH_LEEWAY_S=3600, as_credentials()/from_credentials()), authorization_url(), exchange_authorization_code(), refresh_access_token() (handles the broker ROTATING the refresh token, keeps the old one when the answer omits it), is_expired_token_error(). Endpoints are the real ones (GET https://openapi.ctrader.com/apps/token with QUERY params, id.ctrader.com authorize) and now live in exactly one place. A missing or unparseable token_expires_at is deliberately treated as 'expires now' -- a needless refresh is cheap, a wrong 'still valid' is an outage. (2) bot/clients/ctrader/client.py substantially refactored. It was structurally broken and had never been imported by anything: every public method ran its own reactor.run(), but a Twisted reactor can only run once per OS process, so the SECOND call in a process was impossible. Now the reactor runs ONCE on a module-level daemon thread (_ensure_reactor_running, installSignalHandlers=False, guarded by reactor._startedBefore -- NOT _stopped, which is True before the reactor has ever run) and every public method is a synchronous wrapper over threads.blockingCallFromThread. Each operation is split into a _xxx_step() returning a Deferred plus a thin public wrapper via _call/_blocking_call (CALL_TIMEOUT_S=60, CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S=90), so composite flows cost ONE connect/auth. Added open()/close()/__enter__/__exit__, session-level symbol caching (the old design re-downloaded the whole symbol list on every single call), resolve_symbols()/get_symbols_details()/get_trendbars_many() for portfolio strategies, place_stop_order, and notional= + notional_price= sizing alongside volume_lots= so both the lot-sizing (S007/S021) and dollar-weight (S011) strategies are served by the same methods. Token refresh is PRE-FLIGHT (_ensure_fresh_token runs before the reactor is touched), never retry-on-failure -- a session that dies on an expired token cannot be retried in the same process. close() deliberately does NOT stop the reactor (it cannot be restarted; stopping would break every later client in the process). Fixed a real bug found by the new tests: _load_symbols returned the raw protobuf message on a cold cache but self._symbols on a warm one. (3) bot/ctrader_s011.py rewritten to COMPOSE CTraderApiClient instead of subclassing the legacy CTraderAdapter -- S011 is the first strategy migrated; the others stay on bot/ctrader.py and move over one at a time. All broker protocol code is gone from it; what stayed is genuinely S011's own: the D1 session-date relabelling (D1_SESSION_DATE_ROLL -- the shared client deliberately returns neutral UTC bars), _drop_forming_bar, _last_closed_price (the guard for the 2026-08-19 ~5.7x oversized CAC40 order), and the portfolio-shaped run_live_cycle_multi, which is now plain sequential code inside one `with self.client as broker:`. New public fetch_session_dated_bars() is shared with scripts/s011_check_d1_alignment.py, which no longer needs a private subclass. (4) Credential storage: refresh_token + token_expires_at added to webapp/schemas/accounts.py's CtraderCredentials (both optional -- accounts authorised before this keep working) and to bot/config.py::ctrader_credentials(). NO DB migration needed: credentials_enc is an encrypted JSON dict. webapp/runner.py's THREE duplicated creds-building blocks (S007/S011/S021) collapsed into one _ctrader_creds(acc), and a new _token_persister(session, acc) writes a renewed token back and commits immediately -- passed to S011's cycle via a new on_token_refreshed param threaded through bot/s011_paper.py. Without that callback a refresh is forgotten at cycle end and, once the broker rotates the refresh token, the next cycle would renew with a dead one. (5) scripts/ctrader_oauth.py now delegates to bot/clients/ctrader/auth.py (one implementation of the token endpoints) and gained --db-account, which stores the whole bundle into a webapp Account's encrypted credentials -- the path the scheduled runner actually reads. --write still only patches configs/accounts.yml, which is the single-account CLI path. webapp UI: optional 'Refresh token' field on add_account. (6) Tests: 3 new files, 34 new tests -- tests/bot/test_ctrader_auth.py (refresh grant, rotation, expiry parsing, leeway, expired-token detection), tests/bot/test_ctrader_client_session.py (fake SDK client: lazy/idempotent open, FIVE sequential calls in one process, symbol cache downloaded once, pre-flight refresh reaching the account-auth request, auth rejection surfaced not swallowed), tests/bot/test_ctrader_s011_client.py (session-date relabelling incl. no caller mutation, order priced off the last CLOSED bar, one rejected instrument does not abort the portfolio), tests/webapp/test_runner_ctrader_creds.py (creds merge, commit, round trip).
